before:
name: fieldcv_shared_memory
description: "fieldcv in Field: a Python box runs point tracks and pose over a camera or movie on a worker thread;\
  \ two graphics boxes under agent_graphics_context draw its frames and FLines straight from shared memory. Run\
  \ graphics_renderer_launch first. FIELDCV_SOURCE picks the input (default: the swing from Ballet M\xE9canique)."
operations:
- create:
    box: cv_python_root
    name: python
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 200.0
      w: 200.0
      h: 60.0
    properties:
      mainLanguage: python
- create:
    box: cv_source
    name: fieldcv source
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 300.0
      w: 300.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      code: |
        import os
        import fieldcv as cv4
        from fieldcv import field

        # a sample clip by default; FIELDCV_SOURCE can name a camera index, a movie file or a glob of images
        source = os.environ.get("FIELDCV_SOURCE")
        movie = cv4.open_source(source, loop=True) if source else cv4.sample("swing")
        pose = cv4.Pose(model="lite")
        camera = field.image("camera", 240, 360)
        tracks = field.lines("tracks")
        skeleton = field.lines("skeleton")

        def publish(r):
            camera.write(r["frame"].image)
            tracks.publish(r["tracks"])
            skeleton.publish(cv4.edges(r["poses"], pose.connections))

        p = cv4.Pipeline(movie, cv4.Tracks(), pose, on_result=publish).start()
- connect:
    parent: cv_python_root
    child: cv_source
- wait:
    seconds: 2
- execute:
    box: cv_source
    property: code
    type: fragment
    code: |
      import os
      import fieldcv as cv4
      from fieldcv import field

      # a sample clip by default; FIELDCV_SOURCE can name a camera index, a movie file or a glob of images
      source = os.environ.get("FIELDCV_SOURCE")
      movie = cv4.open_source(source, loop=True) if source else cv4.sample("swing")
      pose = cv4.Pose(model="lite")
      camera = field.image("camera", 240, 360)
      tracks = field.lines("tracks")
      skeleton = field.lines("skeleton")

      def publish(r):
          camera.write(r["frame"].image)
          tracks.publish(r["tracks"])
          skeleton.publish(cv4.edges(r["poses"], pose.connections))

      p = cv4.Pipeline(movie, cv4.Tracks(), pose, on_result=publish).start()
- wait:
    seconds: 2
- create:
    box: cv_camera_quad
    name: camera quad
    frame:
      x: 380.0
      y: 80.0
      w: 280.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      vertex: |
        #version 450
        layout(location = 0) in vec3 pos;
        layout(location = 1) in vec2 tc;
        layout(location = 0) out vec2 ftc;
        void main() { ftc = tc; gl_Position = vec4(pos, 1); }
      fragment: |
        #version 450
        layout(location = 0) in vec2 ftc;
        layout(location = 0) out vec4 uFragColor;
        layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D camera;
        void main() { uFragColor = vec4(texture(camera, ftc).rgb, 1.0); }
      code: |
        import afield.lang.python.NumpyShared
        
        prop<LoadedTexture>(camera) = NumpyShared.image("camera").texture()
        
        var module = moduleHere { }
        var m = Mesh()
        module += m named "camera quad"
        renderer += module
        
        // the image fills the window. Field's NDC is y-up, image v is y-down: v = 0 is the top edge
        m.set(4, 6) {
            pos.add(-1, -1, 0.9,  1, -1, 0.9,  1, 1, 0.9,  -1, 1, 0.9)
            tc.add(0, 1,  1, 1,  1, 0,  0, 0)
            tri.add(0, 1, 2,  0, 2, 3)
        }

- create:
    box: cv_overlay_lines
    name: tracks and skeleton
    frame:
      x: 380.0
      y: 220.0
      w: 280.0
      h: 100.0
    properties:
      vertex: |
        #version 450
        layout(location = 0) in vec3 pos;
        layout(location = 1) in vec4 col;
        layout(location = 0) out vec4 fcol;
        void main() { fcol = col; gl_Position = vec4(pos, 1); }
      fragment: |
        #version 450
        layout(location = 0) in vec4 fcol;
        layout(location = 0) out vec4 uFragColor;
        void main() { uFragColor = fcol; }
      code: |
        import afield.lang.python.NumpyShared
        
        val tracks = NumpyShared.lines("tracks")
        val skeleton = NumpyShared.lines("skeleton")
        
        var module = moduleHere { }
        var m = Mesh()
        module += m named "overlay"
        renderer += module
        
        val width = 0.004   // half the line's width, in NDC: about two pixels across a 1000-pixel window
        
        fun segments(l: List<FLine>) = l.flatMap { it.nodes.zipWithNext() }
        
        frames {
            while (frame()) {
                val segs = segments(tracks.lines()).map { it to vec(0.2, 1.0, 0.3, 1.0) } +
                           segments(skeleton.lines()).map { it to vec(1.0, 0.3, 0.8, 1.0) }
                if (segs.isEmpty()) continue
                // each segment is a thin quad, two triangles, since GPU lines are a single pixel wide
                m.set(4 * segs.size, 2 * segs.size) {
                    for ((i, s) in segs.withIndex()) {
                        val (ab, c) = s
                        // image (u, v), v down, to Field's y-up NDC (2u - 1, 1 - 2v)
                        val ax = 2 * ab.first.to.x - 1
                        val ay = 1 - 2 * ab.first.to.y
                        val bx = 2 * ab.second.to.x - 1
                        val by = 1 - 2 * ab.second.to.y
                        val len = maxOf(Math.hypot((bx - ax).toDouble(), (by - ay).toDouble()), 1e-6)
                        val nx = -(by - ay) / len * width
                        val ny = (bx - ax) / len * width
                        pos.add(ax + nx, ay + ny, 0.1, ax - nx, ay - ny, 0.1, bx - nx, by - ny, 0.1, bx + nx, by + ny, 0.1)
                        4 { col.add(c.x, c.y, c.z, c.w) }
                        tri.add(4 * i, 4 * i + 1, 4 * i + 2, 4 * i, 4 * i + 2, 4 * i + 3)
                    }
                }
            }
        }

              if (segs.isEmpty()) continue

before:
name: fieldcv_webcam_demo
description: "A rich fieldcv starting point: webcam with tracks, pose, hands, face, flow and background subtraction in Python,\
  \ drawn by three Kotlin graphics boxes from shared memory. Creates the boxes; run 0 \xB7 window, then 1 \xB7 webcam, then\
  \ the three Kotlin boxes."
operations:
- create:
    box: cv_renderer
    name: "0 \xB7 window"
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 40.0
      w: 260.0
      h: 60.0
    properties:
      code: "import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options\n\n// 0 · the native window everything below draws into. Run this first.\nprop<Window>(window)\nprop<Renderer>(renderer)\n\nOptions.enableHDR = false\n\nonce.renderer {\n    window = Window(\"fieldcv\")\n    Renderer(window)\n}\n\nstart(renderer::run)\n"
- create:
    box: cv_python
    name: python
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 160.0
      w: 160.0
      h: 40.0
    properties:
      mainLanguage: python
- create:
    box: cv_source
    name: "1 \xB7 webcam + detectors"
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 240.0
      w: 340.0
      h: 120.0
    properties:
      code: "# 1 \xB7 the webcam, and everything fieldcv can find in it\n#\n# Run this once. It starts a Pipeline on a worker\
        \ thread and returns straight away; the\n# frames and everything detected in them go to shared memory under the names\
        \ below, where\n# the graphics boxes on the right read them with NumpyShared.image(...) / .lines(...).\nimport os,\
        \ math\nimport cv2, numpy as np\nimport fieldcv as cv4\nfrom fieldcv import field\n\nH, W = 360, 640             \
        \                       # what we publish; the camera is resized to fit\n\ndef open_input():\n    try:\n        return\
        \ cv4.Camera(0, width=1280, height=720, mirror=True)\n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        movie = os.path.expanduser(\"\
        ~/Desktop/pythonhead/015.mp4\")\n        print(f\"{e} - if macOS asked about the camera, allow it and re-run. Using\
        \ {movie} meanwhile.\")\n        return cv4.Video(movie, loop=True)\n\n# every detector, built once; `use(...)` in\
        \ box 2 chooses which ones run\ndetectors = dict(\n    tracks=cv4.Tracks(length=15, max_tracks=300),\n    pose=cv4.Pose(model=\"\
        lite\"),\n    hands=cv4.Hands(max_hands=2),\n    face=cv4.Face(max_faces=2),\n    flow=cv4.Flow(),\n    background=cv4.Background(\"\
        MOG2\", contours=True, min_area=0.002),\n)\n\ncamera = field.image(\"camera\", H, W)               # the picture,\
        \ full window\ninset = field.image(\"inset\", H, W)                 # a second picture, top right: see `inset_view`\n\
        channels = {n: field.lines(n) for n in [\"tracks\", \"skeleton\", \"hands\", \"face\", \"contours\", \"strokes\"]}\n\
        \n# --- the inset: any function of the frame and the results that returns an image -----------\ndef edges(r):\n  \
        \  return cv2.Canny(cv2.cvtColor(r[\"frame\"].image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY), 60, 140)\n\ndef motion(r):\n    return cv4.Flow.hsv(r[\"\
        flow\"]) if \"flow\" in r else edges(r)\n\ndef mask(r):\n    return r[\"mask\"] if \"mask\" in r else edges(r)\n\n\
        inset_view = edges\n\n# --- pinch to draw: thumb tip (4) near index tip (8) paints, opening your fingers lifts the\
        \ pen\nstrokes, pen_down = [], False\n\ndef draw_with_fingers(r):\n    global pen_down\n    hands = r.get(\"hands\"\
        , np.zeros((0, 21, 3)))\n    if len(hands) == 0:\n        pen_down = False\n        return\n    tip, thumb = hands[0][8,\
        \ :2], hands[0][4, :2]\n    pinched = math.dist(tip * (W, H), thumb * (W, H)) < 0.06 * W\n    if pinched and not pen_down:\n\
        \        strokes.append([])\n    if pinched:\n        strokes[-1].append((tip + thumb) / 2)\n    pen_down = pinched\n\
        \ndef clear():\n    strokes.clear()\n\n# --- called on the worker thread for every frame ------------------------------------------\n\
        def publish(r):\n    camera.write(r[\"frame\"].image)\n    inset.write(inset_view(r))\n    draw_with_fingers(r)\n\
        \    channels[\"tracks\"].publish(r.get(\"tracks\", []))\n    channels[\"skeleton\"].publish(cv4.edges(r[\"poses\"\
        ], detectors[\"pose\"].connections) if \"poses\" in r else [])\n    channels[\"hands\"].publish(cv4.edges(r[\"hands\"\
        ], detectors[\"hands\"].connections) if \"hands\" in r else [])\n    channels[\"face\"].publish(cv4.edges(r[\"faces\"\
        ], detectors[\"face\"].connections) if \"faces\" in r else [])\n    channels[\"contours\"].publish([np.vstack([c,\
        \ c[:1]]) for c in r.get(\"contours\", [])])\n    channels[\"strokes\"].publish([np.asarray(s) for s in strokes if\
        \ len(s) > 1])\n\ndef use(*names):\n    \"\"\"Run just these detectors, e.g. use(\"hands\", \"face\"). The pipeline\
        \ keeps running.\"\"\"\n    p.detectors = [detectors[n] for n in names]\n    return p\n\np = cv4.Pipeline(open_input(),\
        \ on_result=publish)\nuse(\"tracks\", \"pose\", \"hands\", \"face\")\np.start()\n"
- create:
    box: cv_play
    name: "2 \xB7 things to try"
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 400.0
      w: 340.0
      h: 120.0
    properties:
      code: "# 2 \xB7 things to try - select a line and run it (Alt-Enter runs the line under the cursor)\n\nuse(\"hands\"\
        )                                # just hands: pinch thumb and index to draw\nclear()                            \
        \         # wipe the strokes\n\nuse(\"hands\", \"face\", \"pose\")                # landmarks only\nuse(\"tracks\"\
        , \"flow\")                       # motion: point tracks plus dense optical flow\ninset_view = motion            \

name: fieldcv_webcam_demo
description: "A rich fieldcv starting point: webcam with tracks, pose, hands, face, flow and background subtraction in Python,\
  \ drawn by three Kotlin graphics boxes from shared memory. Creates the boxes; run 0 \xB7 window, then 1 \xB7 webcam, then\
  \ the three Kotlin boxes."
operations:
- create:
    box: cv_renderer
    name: "0 \xB7 window"
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 40.0
      w: 260.0
      h: 60.0
    properties:
      code: "import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options\n\n// 0 · the native window everything below draws into. Run this first.\nprop<Window>(window)\nprop<Renderer>(renderer)\n\nOptions.enableHDR = false\n\nonce.renderer {\n    window = Window(\"fieldcv\")\n    Renderer(window)\n}\n\nstart(renderer::run)\n"
- create:
    box: cv_python
    name: python
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 160.0
      w: 160.0
      h: 40.0
    properties:
      mainLanguage: python
- create:
    box: cv_source
    name: "1 \xB7 webcam + detectors"
    frame:
      x: 40.0
      y: 240.0
      w: 340.0
      h: 120.0
    properties:
      code: "# 1 \xB7 the webcam, and everything fieldcv can find in it\n#\n# Run this once. It starts a Pipeline on a worker\
        \ thread and returns straight away; the\n# frames and everything detected in them go to shared memory under the names\
        \ below, where\n# the graphics boxes on the right read them with NumpyShared.image(...) / .lines(...).\nimport os,\
        \ math\nimport cv2, numpy as np\nimport fieldcv as cv4\nfrom fieldcv import field\n\nH, W = 360, 640             \
        \                       # what we publish; the camera is resized to fit\n\ndef open_input():\n    try:\n        return\
        \ cv4.Camera(0, width=1280, height=720, mirror=True)\n    except RuntimeError as e:\n        movie = os.path.expanduser(\"\
        ~/Desktop/pythonhead/015.mp4\")\n        print(f\"{e} - if macOS asked about the camera, allow it and re-run. Using\
        \ {movie} meanwhile.\")\n        return cv4.Video(movie, loop=True)\n\n# every detector, built once; `use(...)` in\
        \ box 2 chooses which ones run\ndetectors = dict(\n    tracks=cv4.Tracks(length=15, max_tracks=300),\n    pose=cv4.Pose(model=\"\
        lite\"),\n    hands=cv4.Hands(max_hands=2),\n    face=cv4.Face(max_faces=2),\n    flow=cv4.Flow(),\n    background=cv4.Background(\"\
        MOG2\", contours=True, min_area=0.002),\n)\n\ncamera = field.image(\"camera\", H, W)               # the picture,\
        \ full window\ninset = field.image(\"inset\", H, W)                 # a second picture, top right: see `inset_view`\n\
        channels = {n: field.lines(n) for n in [\"tracks\", \"skeleton\", \"hands\", \"face\", \"contours\", \"strokes\"]}\n\
        \n# --- the inset: any function of the frame and the results that returns an image -----------\ndef edges(r):\n  \
        \  return cv2.Canny(cv2.cvtColor(r[\"frame\"].image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY), 60, 140)\n\ndef motion(r):\n    return cv4.Flow.hsv(r[\"\
        flow\"]) if \"flow\" in r else edges(r)\n\ndef mask(r):\n    return r[\"mask\"] if \"mask\" in r else edges(r)\n\n\
        inset_view = edges\n\n# --- pinch to draw: thumb tip (4) near index tip (8) paints, opening your fingers lifts the\
        \ pen\nstrokes, pen_down = [], False\n\ndef draw_with_fingers(r):\n    global pen_down\n    hands = r.get(\"hands\"\
        , np.zeros((0, 21, 3)))\n    if len(hands) == 0:\n        pen_down = False\n        return\n    tip, thumb = hands[0][8,\
        \ :2], hands[0][4, :2]\n    pinched = math.dist(tip * (W, H), thumb * (W, H)) < 0.06 * W\n    if pinched and not pen_down:\n\
        \        strokes.append([])\n    if pinched:\n        strokes[-1].append((tip + thumb) / 2)\n    pen_down = pinched\n\
        \ndef clear():\n    strokes.clear()\n\n# --- called on the worker thread for every frame ------------------------------------------\n\
        def publish(r):\n    camera.write(r[\"frame\"].image)\n    inset.write(inset_view(r))\n    draw_with_fingers(r)\n\
        \    channels[\"tracks\"].publish(r.get(\"tracks\", []))\n    channels[\"skeleton\"].publish(cv4.edges(r[\"poses\"\
        ], detectors[\"pose\"].connections) if \"poses\" in r else [])\n    channels[\"hands\"].publish(cv4.edges(r[\"hands\"\
        ], detectors[\"hands\"].connections) if \"hands\" in r else [])\n    channels[\"face\"].publish(cv4.edges(r[\"faces\"\
        ], detectors[\"face\"].connections) if \"faces\" in r else [])\n    channels[\"contours\"].publish([np.vstack([c,\
        \ c[:1]]) for c in r.get(\"contours\", [])])\n    channels[\"strokes\"].publish([np.asarray(s) for s in strokes if\
        \ len(s) > 1])\n\ndef use(*names):\n    \"\"\"Run just these detectors, e.g. use(\"hands\", \"face\"). The pipeline\
        \ keeps running.\"\"\"\n    p.detectors = [detectors[n] for n in names]\n    return p\n\np = cv4.Pipeline(open_input(),\
        \ on_result=publish)\nuse(\"tracks\", \"pose\", \"hands\", \"face\")\np.start()\n"
